benchmark: SPHERIC Test 05 wet-bed dam break d=38 mm
mesh_tools: structured triangle grid, diagonal alternating with the cell parity
notes: The published two-dimensional setup, meshed as a two-dimensional Triangle3 section (decision D51 item 2).
The face files are disjoint: a boundary edge belongs to the wall all of its vertices lie on.

The left, right and bottom walls are free-slip: only the normal velocity is fixed (decision D58); zero surface tension makes this a dam-break transport and impermeability benchmark, not a moving-contact-line wetting validation.
The wall_top face is an open natural-traction boundary with a level-set outflow condition and no velocity Dirichlet condition, matching the open top of the published flume.
The deck approximates the gate as removed instantaneously; the published Test 05 specification raises it at 1.5 m/s.
The initial level-set field is the union of the wet bed and the retained water column; negative values denote the water side.
Pressure uses the local column-height hydrostatic law continued with sign onto dry cut-support vertices; those coefficients are interpolation data, not gas pressure.

qualification_criteria.false_wetting: no vertex with phi < 0 above y = 0.16 m
qualification_criteria.profile_rmse_justification: no regression from the June RMSE of about 0.02 m (0.0184 m d18, 0.0158 m d38 at 0.156 s)

june_three_dimensional_extrusion.stop_on_current_protocol: step 193 (t = 0.0965 s) on the small-cut aggregation guard (root path 9 > 8)
